findings: New raw lines 9-55 establish a single-use wallet, instant provisional access, immediate confirmation, standard payout, B2C not B2B, and distinct merchant/Connect eligibility and customer CN location. Keep the 22-country account list separate from per-account-country presentment currency, with CNY available in every supported country and shown to the buyer. November adds 0.50 USD minimum, explicit domestic and crossborder coverage, applicable Stripe/WeChat business restrictions, complete accessible operational merchant website with products, pricing and checkout and matching business details, and conditional review/reinstatement. Old raw lines 7-55 and 57-83 retain buyer demographic, historical user counts, merchant country list, currency and payout evidence.

New raw lines 73-116 retain no manual capture or disputes, and specify no partial/multi/over capture or listed extended/adjusted authorization types. Refunds remain full/partial, asynchronous and within 180 days. Same-day requests process immediately, later requests batch daily at noon UTC+8, linked-card receipt can take an additional 2-5 days, and refunds cannot be canceled. WeChat refunds to the original funding source rather than reversing the original transaction. Stripe reports `refund.updated`/`refund.failed`; failure returns the amount to the merchant's Stripe balance and requires refund via another method. Old raw lines 116-123 already describe no standard chargeback and refund status and balance consequences.

New raw lines 152-203 preserve mode/invoice/Terminal distinctions and give customer desktop QR scan, eligible native flow launch/return, WeChat app authorization and separate payment-confirmation behavior. The desktop QR checkout stays on the QR screen, and two hours run from creation of the payment request, after which the customer must start a new attempt. Hosted instructions indicate payment success only after a successful payment. For a custom or native flow, the merchant server verifies `PaymentIntent.succeeded` before showing success, independently of return or authorization.

Old raw lines 145-161 and new raw lines 176-177 and 231-237 distinguish destination and separate charges/transfers, private-preview direct and `on_behalf_of` use, standard-Dashboard enablement and platform capability request for connected accounts without standard Dashboard access. November lines 205-223 describe order routing and reconciliation. The settlement merchant's business name, `online` and per-payment descriptor contribute to data sent to WeChat. The platform name applies to destination charges without `on_behalf_of`, the specified connected account with it, and the charge's connected account for direct charges. Buyer-visible registered name and funding statement can differ. Retrieve and expand `latest_charge` and read `latest_charge.payment_method_details.wechat_pay.transaction_id` for reconciliation.

contributions.original_prompts:
New raw `raw/stripe-payments-wechat-pay-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw `raw/stripe-wechat-pay-2025.md`. Current summaries `wiki/sources/source-stripe-wechat-pay.md`.

- Q1. For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/wechat-pay`, what documented behavior, prerequisites, actors and state transitions does the complete new capture establish? How do these compare with the matched prior capture and each mapped summary?

- Q2. Which changes are substantive, presentational or navigation-only? Identify the exact dated qualifications, conflicts and reciprocal routes that the proposed disposition should preserve.

reviewed_answers.Q1: The 2026-11-07 full capture at https://docs.stripe.com/payments/wechat-pay documents a wallet whose eligible B2C merchant enables WeChat Pay, with a working business website and applicable restrictions, and whose Chinese customer authorizes in the WeChat app. New raw lines 9-55, 73-150 and 152-237 distinguish desktop QR authorization within two hours from eligible native-mobile return, server-confirmed PaymentIntent success and standard payout. It retains the old 22 merchant locations, account-mapped currencies, no manual capture or chargeback and asynchronous refunds in old raw lines 8-161, and adds refund timing, noncancellation, two separately gated previews, and Connect descriptor and reconciliation details. source-stripe-wechat-pay.md preserves the basic May behavior but its unconditional recurring exclusion and missing November eligibility, preview and operational boundaries need correction.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/wechat-pay, old raw lines 8-161 and new raw lines 9-237 separate reorganization and navigation from substantive additions such as Stripe/WeChat restrictions, reviewable website and conditional reinstatement review, refund batch/receipt timing, two-hour desktop expiry, Connect descriptors and reconciliation, and off-session recurring and mini-program previews. Preserve November's general unsupported recurring/setup/off-session labels alongside the distinct gated preview prose and API matrix. The cross-method tables change the dated Subscriptions label from supported send_invoice to private preview send_invoice, Terminal from N/A to supported outside Japan, and SetupIntents and future usage from unsupported to private preview. The API matrix redirect label changes from No to Yes. The separate acceptance index links Checkout, Direct API, iOS and Android. Preserve the overview's 22 markets versus the separate May Checkout eligibility list, and distinguish supported native flows from the Mobile Payment Element restriction. Terminal outside Japan appears in both method overviews. source-stripe-wechat-pay.md should retain both full dated captures, the separate acceptance and matrix routes, and reciprocal Stripe index and Wallets concept links.

concept_targets.scope: Audit relevant sections first; only bounded evidence-backed reciprocal corrections in final reviewed findings. No unrelated rewrite.
